stories.deck: It further said that in case of an emergency, Indian nationals could contact the embassy office in Rome at +39 331 614 2085 and the Consulate General of India in Milan at +39 3881647527.
stories.bodyText:
The Indian Embassy in Rome on Monday (October 19, 2026) asked Indian nationals to exercise caution and avoid crowded areas due to protests and demonstrations across several cities in Italy.
The Embassy, in a social media post, said there were protests and demonstrations last week in some Italian cities.
“We advise Indian nationals to exercise caution, avoid crowded areas and locations where protests are taking place and follow local news about such events,” it said.
It further said that in case of an emergency, Indian nationals could contact the embassy office in Rome at +39 331 614 2085 and the Consulate General of India in Milan at +39 3881647527.
The protests against rising cost of living began peacefully across several cities on Sunday. In Milan, rioters clashed with police, looted stores and set property ablaze.
Condemning the violence, Italy’s Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Sunday said, “Demonstrating is a right. Setting our cities ablaze is not.”
“I have great respect for the thousands of people who today demonstrated peacefully... Whatever the ideas for which one demonstrates, participation is the foundation of any healthy democracy,” Ms. Meloni said in a post on X.
The Italian premier said stones were thrown at the law enforcement forces in Milan, which led to injuries to officers and forced the interruption of the procession.
She said people carrying cobblestones and hammers were stopped in Turin and a railway station was closed as a precautionary measure in Bologna.
Ms. Meloni requested the opposition to unequivocally condemn these acts of violence and issue a clear appeal for every mobilisation to be peaceful.
The protests in Italy coincided with nationwide protests in neighbouring France against rising living costs and in support of high school students’ grievances.

stories.headline: Migrants have taken over France, they must close the borders: Trump on France riots
stories.deck: At a rally in Kansas, the U.S. President launched into a lengthy tirade about France, which he said was being “conquered, looted, and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists, and communists”
stories.bodyText:
U.S. President Donald Trump used the protests roiling France to score some quick political points on Monday (October 19, 2026), as the upcoming midterm elections force his Republican party to face strong headwinds.
At a rally in Kansas, the U.S. President launched into a lengthy tirade about France, which he said was being “conquered, looted, and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists, and communists.”
“And we’re not going to let that happen to this country,” he added.
While speaking with reporters previously in the day, Mr. Trump recalled an exchange with his French counterpart Emmanuel Macron: “I told him a long time ago, you’re making a big mistake in France. You’re letting everybody from the world come in...Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon.”
Earlier on Monday (October 19, 2026), the 80-year-old President wrote on his Truth Social platform: “The migrants have taken over France. They must CLOSE THE BORDERS, FAST!”
Cost-of-living demonstrations broke out across France over the weekend, with many devolving into looting and violent conflict, prompting officials to institute partial curfews on Monday (October 19, 2026).
While the French protests were inspired by soaring inflation, Trump has molded the violent clashes with police into evidence in favor of the anti-immigration policies he used to successfully campaign for reelection in 2024.
“They’re taking this French crisis and turning it into a campaign argument,” J.C. Lintzenich, a senior fellow with the German Marshall Fund think tank, told AFP.
Conservative talking points
Opinion polls heavily favour Mr. Trump’s rival Democratic Party in the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine who will take control of Congress.
With just two weeks to go before Americans go to the polls, Mr. Trump has grasped any strategy he can to compel voters to support the Republican party and his Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement.
“Since the beginning of the MAGA movement, Europe has been an extension of the US political battlefield, so it’s not surprising that when there are events like the unrest from October 17, the political machine gets moving,” Justin Vaisse, a professor of U.S. foreign policy at Johns Hopkins University, told AFP.
As videos of France’s unrest began surfacing on social media, Vice President J.D. Vance wrote Saturday (October 17, 2026) on X: “Western liberals imported the third world into France...they ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility.”
Right-wing U.S. media personalities, including Glenn Beck, Benny Johnson, Nick Sortor and Jack Posobiec made similar points, blaming immigrants from Muslim-majority countries for causing a crisis in Western identity.
“The riots are viewed as validation of the warnings against immigration in general and Muslim immigration, if such a thing exists,” Vaisse said.
Celia Belin, a senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations and head of its Paris office, views the commentary as an “export of domestic policies” from a US administration that openly supports nationalist parties in Europe.
She told AFP that Mr. Trump and his allies “rushed into this argument, the same one that Vance had presented in Munich” in 2025, in a controversial speech described as a US culture war against Europe, with the goal of “fanning the flames.”
Polling priorities
Experts note that this rhetorical strategy, while it may have succeeded in 2024, is not necessarily what US voters want to hear these days.
“When you look at the campaign ads here — I’m in South Carolina right now -- it’s about healthcare, domestic issues,” Lintzenich said.
“The international element is a blip on the radar, and Ukraine, and Iran, and other ongoing national security issues rate higher than the current French instability,” he continued.
A Pew Research poll this month found the economy plays an important role in the choice of 82% of U.S. voters, a far higher number than immigration (59%) or race-related issues (36%).
Though Mr. Trump has followed through on his 2024 campaign promise to crack down on immigration, he has fared less successfully on his other promise to tamp down on inflation, with his tariff policies and war with Iran spiking prices across the economy, plunging his approval rating to record lows.
Vaisse said using linking U.S. identitarian rhetoric with the events in France “is not going to win a single vote” for Republicans, though it could “mobilize the base” to vote.

stories.headline: ‘You’ll see soon enough’: Trump on efforts to free US hostage held in Russia
stories.deck: Donald Trump suggested a potential breakthrough in the release of an American hostage held by Russia. He underscored the necessity of maintaining open communication with Russian President Vladimir Putin on various issues. Trump noted advancements in negotiations concerning the Ukraine conflict, energy supplies, and the hostage situation, while cautioning that he could step back from discussions…
stories.bodyText:
US president Donald Trump has hinted at a possible breakthrough in efforts to secure the release of an American hostage held in Russia. He also defended his decision to keep diplomatic negotiations with Russian president Vladimir Putin open on Ukraine, Iran, energy pipelines and hostages.
Speaking to reporters outside the White House on Monday (local time), Trump said he was seeking the release of a hostage whose case had remained unresolved for years, suggesting that progress could emerge soon.
“Well, you’ll see soon enough, because I’m trying to get a hostage that the country’s been after for a long time, and before my time,” Trump said when asked what assurances Putin had given that he wanted to reach a deal. “And let’s see what happens, that’ll be—that’ll be soon.”
Trump’s remarks followed his statement on Sunday that negotiations to end the Russia-Ukraine conflict were making “great progress”. He defended his approach towards Moscow, arguing that imposing further penalties could undermine ongoing talks.
“My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “Great progress is being made, and that includes current hostage negotiations!”
He added, “Signing that document at this time will do that, and I can sign it later, or any time that I want!”
Earlier, Trump had signaled that he was willing to hold a high-stakes trilateral meeting with Putin and Chinese president Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine and pursuing global denuclearisation, even if Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy was excluded from the negotiations. 
“Anything I can do to end the war, whether somebody’s there or not", he said.
Trump also cited Russia’s limited support for Iran amid escalating US economic and military pressure on Tehran as a reason to continue engaging with Moscow.
"Russia could have done a lot more to help, if you put it bluntly, Russia could have done a lot more to help Iran. Russia has done very little for Iran, and China could have done a lot more for Iran. They’ve done, and I remember that. When China does not that much, maybe nothing almost, but very little for Iran, and Russia does very little for Iran, I view that as being a very positive thing", he said.
He added, “Russia’s done nothing there that we could see, and I think that’s a very positive.”
Defending the broader negotiations, Trump said Washington was also discussing energy supplies and pipelines with Moscow, warning that he could withdraw from the process if the talks failed to deliver results.
“And of course, we’re negotiating with him on Ukraine. So, I’m not looking to break up negotiations right in the middle,” he said. “And by the way, I have the right to do that at any time immediately. So if things don’t work out, I can always do it.”
Trump’s outreach to Moscow has drawn criticism from some Republican lawmakers, particularly over sanctions and energy-related discussions. He said several lawmakers had contacted him after learning more about the negotiations

briefs.headline: Gold mine collapse kills at least 14 in southwest Colombia
briefs.deck: At least six miners were killed Monday when an open-pit gold mine collapsed in a remote corner of Colombia’s Nariño province, authorities said
briefs.bodyText:
At least 14 miners were killed when an open-pit gold mine operating with no permits collapsed in a remote corner of Colombia’s Nariño province, regional authorities said.
In a statement, Nariño’s government said an additional seven people were injured in the mining accident on Monday near the small town of Santa Barbara de Iscuande, adding that search efforts had ended Monday night.
“This emergency once again highlights the risks associated with informal mining,” the statement said. “In less than three months, two collapsed mines in Nariño have killed 27 people.”
Santa Barbara de Iscuande is surrounded by dense rainforest and can only be reached by boat or small aircraft, which makes it difficult for aid workers to reach the area.
“Entire families have been killed in this regrettable accident. It is very sad,” said Nariño’s governor, Luis Alfonso Escobar.
Hundreds of small mines in Colombia operate without government permits, and some are controlled by rebel groups.
Besides being difficult to reach, Santa Barbara de Iscuande also faces security problems.
Two rebel groups reportedly operate in the area, including the Jacobo Arenas Block, a group led by former members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) who refused to join a 2016 peace deal with Colombia’s government.
In a statement, Colombia’s Ombudsman’s Office urged armed groups in the area to allow humanitarian aid to reach the small town.
“All of our efforts must go towards protecting lives and tending to this emergency,” the office said on X.

briefs.headline: France protests: Paris police issue overnight curfew in two areas to try to prevent further disorder
briefs.deck: The curfew prohibits anyone from entering or remaining on the Place de la République, where rioting took place, and the shopping neighbourhood of Les Halles
briefs.bodyText:
Paris police issued an overnight curfew in two areas of the French capital, after a weekend marred by France's worst rioting in years that targeted city halls, other public buildings and thousands of businesses across the country.
The order issued on Monday (October 19, 2026) aims to protect “people and property from the violence and looting”, the Paris police statement said.
The curfew prohibits anyone from entering or remaining on the Place de la République, where rioting took place Saturday (October 17, 2026), and the shopping neighbourhood of Les Halles, which has been subject to looting.
The curfew will be in effect from 11 pm on Monday until 6 am on Tuesday. In addition, gatherings and demonstrations are banned from 8 pm, the Paris police said.
Earlier Monday (October 19, 2026), Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu had called for “very limited” and “localised” curfews.
In northern France, local authorities imposed a curfew for children and teenagers under age 18 in several cities, including Lille, starting from Monday (October 19, 2026) and for the next two days from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Nice, on the French Riviera, also imposed an overnight curfew for minors from 9 p.m.
Mr. Lecornu defended police handling of the unrest, saying that “despite scenes of severe violence and extensive property damage, no one was killed, and that is a miracle”.
He said that details of the curfews would be announced later Monday (October 19, 2026) after consultations with mayors.
Mass protests in France are often tainted by violence on the fringes of otherwise peaceful marches, leading to clashes with police. Saturday's unrest recalled the riots that followed the fatal police shooting of a teenager in 2023, when authorities imposed local curfews, and violence during the yellow vest movement that began in 2018 over fuel prices and broader economic grievances.

briefs.headline: Young innovators impress juries with ideas to solve real-world challenges
briefs.bodyText:
Jury members evaluate entries for TOI’s Ideas for India contest in Delhi
NEW DELHI: Three separate juries evaluated entries in the three categories for the award and the panel members acknowledged at the end of the day that the quality of applicants was excellent. In each of the categories, bulk of those shortlisted for evaluation by the jury were very young, either still in college or just out of it, though there were some older innovators too.
The maturity to take hard questions as essential inputs rather than as harsh criticism was quite remarkable.
Ideas For India
The diversity of the presentations was also a striking aspect. In the technology sovereignty category, for instance, the ideas ranged from closing a felt gap in middle sized drones to faster and more efficient identification and countering of cyberattacks to dealing with ships that go ‘dark’, which may not always be for innocent reasons.
But these were not just ideas. The drone entry had already done some testing in the field with army units, the dark ships idea had been explored with a port and so on.

Food quality on trains to get better? IRCTC and QCI to crack down with surprise audits
briefs.deck: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Limited (IRCTC) has entered into a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Quality Council of India to strengthen compliance with food safety and hygiene standards across the railway system, according to a statement issued by the Railway Ministry. As part of the system, inspectors will use a mobile application to record their findings, with…
briefs.bodyText:
The food quality on trains may see an improvement with the Quality Council of India (QCI) looking to appoint certified professionals to carry out independent, technology-enabled checks of food safety and hygiene at railway stations and aboard trains across the 
Indian Railways
 network.
Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Limited (
IRCTC
) has entered into a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with QCI to strengthen compliance with food safety and hygiene standards across the railway system, according to a statement issued by the Railway Ministry
"Under this strategic alliance, QCI will deploy certified professionals to conduct intense, unannounced quarterly and half-yearly inspection cycles," the ministry said.
It added: "These audits will enforce strict compliance with statutory Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) regulations and international culinary standards."
Addressing passenger complaints on food
Officials said the decision to introduce independent inspections followed repeated passenger complaints about poor food quality and unhygienic catering practices. The ministry subsequently decided to bring in a third-party agency to audit food safety and hygiene.
"To eliminate data tampering and guarantee absolute transparency, the audit process will leverage QCI's pioneer digital infrastructure," the ministry said.
As part of the system, inspectors will use a mobile application to record their findings, with geo-tagging, time-stamps and photographic evidence made mandatory.
Audit reports will have to be submitted within 24 hours, allowing operational shortcomings to be identified promptly and enabling corrective and preventive measures to be tracked against vendors found violating the prescribed standards.
Explaining how the initiative would benefit passengers, the ministry said: "Rigorous independent screening across trains ensures passengers are protected from subpar onboard meal preparation."
It also highlighted the need for uniform hygiene standards at station-based catering facilities, stating: "Complete standardisation guarantees immaculate cooking environments across all major station-based static units," the ministry added.
The ministry said the use of digitally documented evidence and the requirement to submit reports within 24 hours would help speed up corrective action and the imposition of penalties against catering licensees where necessary.
IRCTC Food checks
Indian Railways serves an average of around 58 crore meals annually. Over the past three years, IRCTC has taken punitive action in response to complaints against several vendors.
According to a recent PIB release, these measures include imposing fines of Rs 5.13 crore, issuing 54 show-cause notices, terminating six contracts and debarring licensees for violations related to food quality and hygiene. IRCTC has made the list of debarred licensees available on its website.
Railway and IRCTC officials, including Food Safety Officers, carry out routine as well as surprise inspections to check food quality, hygiene, safety and compliance with applicable regulations.
These inspections examine several aspects of catering operations, including food safety, staff deployment, upkeep of equipment, cleanliness and adherence to prescribed standards. They also seek to encourage best practices in food handling, storage and preparation.
According to Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s recent reply to a question in Rajya Sabha, IRCTC is taking the following measures on food quality:
- Providing meals that are prepared at designated base kitchens.
- Setting up modern base kitchens at some select locations.
- Installing CCTV cameras in base kitchens that enables real-time surveillance and improves the monitoring of food preparation.
- Identifying and using popular branded raw materials for preparing food.
- Appointing Food Safety Supervisors at base kitchens to oversee food safety and hygienic practices.
- Deploying IRCTC supervisors on board trains.
- Carrying out deep cleaning at regular intervals and conducting periodic pest-control activities in base kitchens and pantry cars.

briefs.headline: ‘Zelenskyy should get someone else’: Trump open to Putin-Xi talks on Ukraine war
briefs.bodyText:
US President Donald Trump on Monday said he was open to holding trilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, while suggesting that Ukraine should have someone else negotiate on its behalf in the war with Russia.
Asked whether he would meet Putin and Xi without Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump said: “Anything I can do to end the war, whether somebody’s there or not.”
Trump said the proposed meeting would primarily focus on nuclear weapons and denuclearisation, although trade and other issues could also be discussed.
“We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearization,” Trump told reporters outside the White House. “If President Xi wants to have it, I'd have it.”
The remarks came after the Kremlin said a possible trilateral meeting had been discussed and could take place on the sidelines of next month’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China. The meeting has not been formally confirmed.
Trump questions Zelenskyy’s role in negotiations
Trump renewed his criticism of Zelenskyy, arguing that the Ukrainian leader should have reached a settlement with Russia earlier and questioning his handling of the conflict.
“Zelenskyy doesn’t know what he’s talking about,” Trump said, responding to the Ukrainian president’s criticism of the US administration.
“To be honest, I don't think—I think it’s time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine, because what’s happened, very little land has moved, but a million people, a tremendous number of people are dead,” Trump asserted. “They’re losing their male population. Ukraine could have had this thing settled a long time ago if he would have listened to me, and you remember the Oval Office, he would have had this settled a long time ago. Maybe it’s time for Zelenskyy to get somebody else to negotiate.”
Trump’s comments come amid growing tensions between Washington and Kyiv over US policy towards Russia, including the easing of certain sanctions and concerns over disruptions to Ukraine’s satellite communications and intelligence-sharing arrangements.
Putin’s reported proposal for trilateral summit
The Wall Street Journal reported that Putin had proposed a trilateral summit with Trump and Xi during an October 9 phone call with the US president. The meeting could take place during the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, scheduled for November 18 and 19, the report said.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told the newspaper that discussions about a possible meeting were underway, but there was no clear understanding of the meeting or its agenda.
Trump said he would be willing to participate if Xi supported the proposal, describing denuclearisation as a key objective. He also indicated that the leaders could discuss trade.
The potential summit has raised questions about Ukraine’s representation in discussions over the war. Zelenskyy has also said that a possible trilateral meeting involving Putin could take place in the United States during the G20 summit in December, although confirmation from Moscow and Washington was still awaited.

stories.headline: Car not a toy, says HC; dad to face trial for crash by minor that killed 3
stories.deck: Following a devastating incident, a father contested the Karnataka high court's ruling regarding culpable homicide charges linked to his 14-year-old son's reckless driving. The accident claimed three lives, leading the court to stress the perils of allowing minors to operate vehicles and affirm the importance of parents being accountable. The father's attempt to cancel the charges was ultimately…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A car cannot become a toy in the hands of underage children, Karnataka high court observed, refusing to quash culpable homicide proceedings against a Mysuru resident whose 14-year-old son caused an accident that left three members of a family dead in Dec 2020.
"The steering wheel of a motor vehicle cannot become a plaything in the hands of a child, nor can a public road become the playground for such indulgence," Justice M Nagaprasanna observed in his order dated Oct 16, stressing that parental responsibility cannot be evaded when a minor is willingly allowed to drive.
The petitioner's son was driving a Volkswagen Vento, entrusted to his father by his employer, when the accident took place on old Bengaluru-Mysuru road, killing a couple and their five-year-old son.
The petitioner, Nadeem-Ur-Rehman, had challenged the rejection of his discharge plea by a trial court and had sought the quashing of proceedings against him under IPC section 304 Part-II, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder. He was also facing allegations of other traffic violations.
Karnataka recorded 751 accidents involving minors in 2025-26
The petitioner contended that his son took the vehicle out without his knowledge. 
The case could, at best, be an offence based on rashness or negligence, but could not be elevated to culpable homicide, he further argued.
Opposing the plea, the public prosecutor submitted that the material on record indicated the petitioner had handed the car keys to his son and permitted him to drive. He said this had allegedly happened on earlier occasions as well.
A parent who knowingly hands car keys to a child cannot “retreat behind the minority of that child when the adventure ends in catastrophe”, HC observed. The question of whether a parent’s conduct was negligence or culpable knowledge could be decided at the trial, it said. Quoting statistics, Justice Nagaprasanna noted that Karnataka recorded 751 accidents involving minors in 2025-26, standing at sixth place among all states.

stories.headline: Karnataka Public Service Commission recruitment row: Supreme Court reserves order, seeks affidavits by Oct 26
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The 
Supreme Court
 has reserved its order on a challenge to Karnataka high court’s refusal to entertain a 2022 PIL against a state law validating the recruitment of 362 gazetted probationers by Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) in 2011.
A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and Vinod Chandran said: “Arguments concluded, judgment reserved… As discussed, both sides shall file their respective affidavits, providing a break-up by Oct 26. In the facts of this case, we permit the applicants who are seeking impleadment/intervention in the present proceeding also to file a brief note in the applications pending as on date.”
The govt had cancelled the recruitment in 2013 following 
CID
 reports of corruption and irregularities. Some selected candidates approached Karnataka Administrative Tribunal (KAT) and secured appointments. The HC subsequently set aside KAT’s order, a decision upheld by SC.
In 2022, the state enacted a law validating the entire selection process. The HC dismissed a challenge to the legislation on April 21, 2022, observing that the petitioners had failed to establish that any provision was unconstitutional, illegal or void.
The unsuccessful candidates then approached SC. Senior counsel Shyam Divan, appearing for the petitioners, argued that the recruitment was vitiated by irregularities. 
He submitted that 566 candidates had secured identical marks and that examination records were subsequently destroyed.
Sahukar, Geeta sent to 14-day judicial custody
A special court in Bengaluru Monday remanded suspended KPSC chairperson Shivashankarappa Sahukar and member BV Geeta in judicial custody for 14 days.
Enforcement Directorate
 had on Oct 6 arrested the two for alleged involvement in the job-for-cash scam. On Monday afternoon, ED sleuths produced Sahukar and Geeta before the special court and later took them to Bengaluru central prison in a police jeep.
CID seeks sanction to prosecute IAS officer
CID has sought govt sanction to prosecute suspended IAS officer Gangwar, arrested over his alleged involvement in leaking questions for a KPSC recruitment exam. The move follows SC’s recent direction to the SIT to continue its probe along the lines of the CID investigation.
A senior CID officer said the latest law provides that if govt does not respond within 120 days, sanction is deemed granted.

stories.headline: The Howdah Bearers | Mysuru's Dasara elephants
stories.deck: Kings stopped riding it in 1969. The elephants never stopped carrying it. This year, Mysuru has picked the next elephant.
stories.bodyText:
Mysuru Dasara · from the The Hindu archives
The Howdah Bearers
The Elephant carrying the golden howdah is the highlight of the grand Dasara festival in Mysuru. Kings stopped riding in the howdah in 1969, but the elephants never stopped carrying it. This year, Mysuru has picked the next elephant, Prashantha. Walk through The Hindu's archives with us to explore the journey of the famous Dasara elephants.
Scroll
Every year, during the Dasara festival, a grand procession is undertaken from the Mysuru Palace to the Bannimantap Parade Grounds. The chief attraction of this parade is an elephant decked out in splendour, carrying the golden howdah.
The howdah started out as a structure originally meant for Mysuru's kings to ride in. However, the Mysuru maharaja stopped riding in them in 1969. Even so, the elephants never stopped carrying it. This year, a new elephant replaced the old one, and the tradition continues.
But first, before the parade, the elephants undertake a journey from the forests. Here is how it begins.
In August, the elephants walked in from the forests of Nagarahole. This is called the Gajapayana, the elephants' journey.
Once in Mysuru, they march five kilometres twice a day, from the palace to Bannimantap, to learn the route and get used to the din.
For the trial exercise, they carry a wooden copy of the howdah. Mahendra's load comes to nearly 850 kg.
The load on their backs grows, day by day, in preparation for the weight of the howdah.
1000kg may seem like a lot to bear, but to put the weight in perspective, let's look at the weights of some Dasara elephants.
On the third round of the trial exercise, Mahendra stops and will not go on.
Four elephants are left, Dhananjaya, Sugreeva, Ekalavya and Prashantha.
On Vijayadashami, one of them, Prashantha, was chosen to carry the real howdah.
This is the golden howdah.
It weighs 750 kg.
What sits inside it today is a bronze idol of the goddess Chamundeshwari. It weighs not more than 10 kg.
So why is the seat at least 75 times heavier than its current passenger?
Because it was built for a king.
750 kg
10 kg
However, it did not always have a king in it. Over the years, the howdah's occupant has changed.
The king got off.
The weight stayed on.
A fitting adieu
Mysuru's Dasara elephants are no less decorated after the procession than during it. Their passing is mourned deeply by their mahouts, and the State pays high honours.
After their years of service carrying the howdah, the Dasara elephants are remembered with fondness and respect after their passing.
Drona, 1997. Reaching for a branch in the forest, he touched a high-tension wire.
Balarama, 2023. Died at his camp, aged 67. He had a huge fan following and his very own Wikepedia entry.
Arjuna, 2023. Killed fighting a wild tusker. Vinod, his mahout, was inconsolable at his funeral and could be seen trying to wake him up, evoking the emotions of the crowd.
Three rounds were fired in the air.
Gun salutes used to be for kings.

stories.headline: Garbage truck driver booked for running over stray puppy at Avalahalli in Bengaluru
stories.deck: The complainant alleges that the garbage vehicle’s driver, Chakku Miah, failed to honk or make any apparent attempt to alert the dog before running over the animal
stories.bodyText:
Avalahalli police in Bengaluru have registered a case against the driver of a garbage collection vehicle for allegedly running over and killing a 10-month-old female stray dog at Konadasapura village on October 16.
According to the complaint filed by Veena N., a resident of Seetharayya Road in Konadasapura village, the incident occurred around 7.44 a.m. when the puppy was sitting by the roadside.
The complainant alleges that the garbage vehicle’s driver, Chakku Miah, failed to honk or make any apparent attempt to alert the dog before running over the animal.
Even after the vehicle hit the puppy, the driver allegedly did not stop and ran over the animal again, killing it on the spot.
People who witnessed the incident reportedly told the driver to stop. They told him not to move the vehicle after noticing the puppy trapped beneath the truck.
However, the driver allegedly ignored their warnings, and moved the vehicle.
Avalahalli police have registered a case under Cruelty to Animals Act, and also under Section 325 of BNS.

briefs.headline: Inaugural Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper run likely on Nov 1
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: South Western Railway has proposed to run the inaugural special of Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express on Nov 1, coinciding with Karnataka Rajyotsava.
However, the date for commencement of regular commercial services is yet to be notified. SWR sources said railway minister 
Ashwini Vaishnaw
 is expected to flag off the train, which will be the first Vande Bharat sleeper service in southern India.
The train (27651/27652) will have 16 coaches — 11 AC three-tier, four AC two-tier and one AC first-class coach — with a total capacity of 823 berths.
Sources said the fare for the 1,118-km journey between Bengaluru and 
Mumbai
 could range from Rs 2,600 to Rs 4,250, depending on the class of travel. The final fare structure is yet to be announced.
The new service is expected to significantly reduce travel time between the two cities, a route that has long lacked a faster overnight rail connection. The existing Udyan Express, the principal daily direct train between the two cities, takes around 24 hours to complete the journey. The proposed Vande Bharat Sleeper is expected to cover the distance in about 16 hours.
The proposed route will pass through Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Solapur and Kalyan before reaching Mumbai.
An official said the service could not be launched in Oct because the model code of conduct was in force for Karnataka legislative council elections.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru North corporation seeks citizen participation to plug waste management gaps
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Bengaluru North City Corporation has urged citizens to help identify gaps in solid waste management, particularly unauthorised collection of bulk waste by domestic door-to-door collection vehicles. The practice overloads auto tippers, forcing them to make multiple trips to unload waste and disrupting collection from designated households.
Corporation officials have observed cases of bulk waste generators handing over waste to domestic collection vehicles instead of authorised bulk waste transporters. Commissioner Pommala Sunil Kumar said citizens could report such violations to the corporation, which would initiate action against defaulting bulk waste generators.
Citizens can report the violations on the special phone-in programme held on Tuesdays, specifically for solid waste management issues, by contacting 9480685705 or 080-22975936/23636671.
BNCC has identified 1,299 bulk waste generators (BWGs), of which 182 have registered with Central Pollution Control Board, and 48 have in-situ waste processing facilities. Bulk waste generators include those that generate over 100kg of waste per day, apartments with over 100 units, those that consume over 40,000 litres of water per day, or properties over 5,000 sqm in area (or 20,000 sqm built-up area).
RWA participation
The corporation has also urged resident welfare associations (RWAs) to monitor waste management operations, including attendance and timings of personnel at mustering points. Each ward has two such points — one for pourakarmikas and another for garbage collection vehicles. The commissioner said officials had been instructed to facilitate citizen access to these points to improve accountability.
Residents can scan division-wise QR codes on the corporation’s social media handles to access contact details of the auto-tipper driver and supervisor assigned to their block. Residents will be able to see which auto-tipper collects waste and which pourakarmikas have been assigned to a particular road. The purpose of the system is to facilitate citizens in coordinating with SWM personnel and handling waste responsibly instead of resorting to littering.
“Apart from the micro plan, we have also pressed into service four Prahari vehicles to target stretches prone to garbage dumping. The vehicles are fitted with dashcams and send updates to our officials on illegal dumping. This helps them clear the spots and identify gaps in door-to-door collection,” Kumar said.
Following the transfer of waste collection and transportation responsibilities from Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Ltd (BSWML) to city corporations in Aug, BNCC has prepared division-wise micro plans based on local requirements. Around 750 to 1,000 households have been mapped to each auto tipper, with designated routes based on the number of households, road network, waste collection requirements and time needed to complete the route.

briefs.headline: Rabbit on Bengaluru airport runway? Nah, it’s all clear, says probe
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Rabbit, foreign object or just hazy notions? Two days after an Air India Express flight IX 2004 aborted its initial landing attempt at Kempegowda International Airport, its operator has clarified that neither a foreign object nor an animal was spotted on the runway.
The flight, which departed Goa at 6.48pm, reached Bengaluru around 8pm and was about to touch down at KIA. Sources aware of the situation Sunday told 
TOI that while descending, the pilot got instructions from Air Traffic Control for a go-around.
While the exact reason is yet to be examined, the ATC communicated to the flight that there was a foreign object present on the runway. A few minutes later, he executed a safe landing, and everything was normal, the source added.
On Monday, KIA’s operator Bangalore International Airport (BIAL) stated that the situation happened due to an alert by an 
IndiGo
 flight. A BIAL official told TOI that the IndiGo pilot, while landing around 8pm Saturday, thought he saw a rabbit on the runway. BIAL confirmed not even a small foreign object had appeared on the runway.
“Our apron team checked and cleared for landing following which the next flight landed,” the official said, adding the pilot had made an in-flight announcement on the presence of an animal while executing a go-around, which fuelled the argument.

briefs.headline: Milk of anger: No Dasara bonus, farmers pour hundreds of litres at society in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Dairy farmers poured hundreds of litres of milk onto the floor of a milk cooperative society in Narayanapura, Nelamangala taluk, on Monday, protesting non-payment of Dasara incentives and govt subsidies and alleging financial irregularities.
The farmers said they had reached the cooperative around 5am to deliver milk, but waited for more than two-and-a-half hours without any resolution from the management. Around 7.30am, they emptied milk cans across the premises in protest.
They accused the Narayanapura Milk Producers Cooperative Society’s management of repeatedly promising to release the annual Dasara bonus but failing to do so. They also alleged mismanagement of govt incentive payments and financial irregularities involving members’ savings.
“We labour hard to keep the dairy supply running, but when festival time comes, the authorities play games with our hard-earned bonus and savings,” said protesting farmer Manjappa.
The protesters demanded an inquiry and audit of the cooperative’s functioning, directing their anger at society president 
Manjunath
, the secretary and other board members.
Society president Manjunath was unavailable for comment. The farmers warned they would intensify their agitation and approach district cooperative department officials if their pending bonuses and savings were not released immediately.

briefs.headline: Tomato prices crash up to 80% in Bengaluru; drop is not city-wide
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Price of kitchen staple tomato has crashed from Rs 50 a kg to as low as Rs 10 in about a week, but the relief is not uniform across varieties. Different parts of the city quoted different price points during a 
TOI dipstick survey.
Glut in production, slow offtake and tapering of demand were cited as reasons behind the price crash. The city gets its tomatoes from within 
Karnataka
 and 
Tamil Nadu
. In Karnataka, Kolar is the biggest producer with around 15,000 acres, and the crop is exported to northern states and neighbouring countries like Bangladesh.
Tomatoes on multiple online platforms are listed at Rs 30-40 a kg, depending on variety, size and quality.
A vegetable vendor from South End Circle said the per-kg price has gone down from Rs 50 to Rs 30 in four days and the demand for tomatoes has also gone down from the customers during the festive season.
Another vegetable vendor from Basavanagudi said that the price has declined to Rs 40, Rs 30 and even Rs 20 for some in the past one week, depending on the quality and variety. “We saw rainfall a few days ago. Despite the festival demand, the market is still left with plenty of stock. That’s why prices have come down.”
However, multiple vendors in Koramangala said prices have stayed in the Rs 25-35 range for quite some time and they have not seen any sudden drop.

briefs.headline: NGT halts tree felling for Hebbal Short Tunnel Project in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: The tribunal has scheduled the next hearing for December 15
briefs.bodyText:
The National Green Tribunal (NGT) on Friday issued an order restraining the felling of trees for the Hebbal Short Tunnel Project until the hearing is completed and the matter is disposed of.
The NGT order states: “There should not be any cutting of trees, be it in any area of the Hebbal Short Tunnel Project till the matter is disposed of.”
The tribunal has scheduled the next hearing for December 15. This also means that the BDA cannot cut any trees along the Hebbal Short Tunnel alignment till mid-December.
The order followed a petition filed by a civic group, subsequent to the NGT taking suo motu cognisance of The Hindu’s report on the Bangalore Development Authority’s (BDA) proposal to remove trees for the Hebbal Short Tunnel Project. The report, dated September 24, was titled “Over 70 tree species among 1,128 marked for felling for Hebbal tunnel project in Bengaluru”.
In the suo motu case, the Karnataka government submitted a representation stating that writ petitions concerning the matter were pending before the High Court, where the Advocate-General had given an undertaking that no trees would be cut until the matter was disposed of. Subsequently, the NGT disposed of the original suo motu case.
However, Aranya, Parisara Mathu Havamana Badalavane, Sangha, Mangaluru, noticed a discrepancy and filed another application seeking a restraining order. The group brought to the NGT’s notice that the undertaking given by the Advocate-General before the Karnataka High Court, as stated during the suo motu hearing, pertained to a different area — Lalbagh — though it was for the same project.
“This original application, in general, covers the entire project and felling of trees for the same,” the NGT order said. Counsel representing the government also clarified that the undertaking pertained to a different area.
Subsequently, the NGT passed the Friday order.
Meanwhile, BDA Chairman N. A. Haris, in a conversation with The Hindu, said that the BDA does not intend to fell all 1,128 trees but instead plans to translocate 1,072 trees and axe the remaining ones. However, the public notice issued by the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) refers to the “removal” of trees along Hebbal Main Road for the 2.3-km twin tunnel project.
On the other hand, civic groups opposing the short tunnel project argue that the BDA cannot announce such a decision, as it can be taken only by the Tree Expert Committee.

briefs.headline: Karnataka extends ration card e-KYC deadline to November 10
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka government has extended the deadline for e-KYC verification of ration card beneficiaries to November 10 from October 20, according to a press release from the Department of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs.
The extension follows an order requiring 1,15,87,298 beneficiaries who completed e-KYC more than a year ago to undergo the verification again.
The department said 3,82,362 beneficiaries who have never completed e-KYC and 54,27,396 whose last verification was more than five years ago also remain to be verified.
All these beneficiaries must complete the e-KYC by November 10, either through the ‘Anna Seva’ mobile application or at fair price shops using the AHARA software. Failure to comply could invite further action under the rules, the release said.
App available across India
The department has extended the availability of the Anna Seva app across the country to help Karnataka ration cardholders who have moved to other States for work complete the process without returning to Karnataka.
Such beneficiaries can download the app and complete the e-KYC from their current location. An updated version of the app is available on the Google Play Store. Those who have already downloaded it can update it to the latest version, the department said.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru metro commuters raise questions over unused balance in smart cards as NCMC adoption grows
briefs.bodyText:
As more commuters shift to National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) following its acceptance on Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) buses, questions are being raised over the unused balance in existing Namma Metro smart cards.
Commuters who have used the metro traditional smart cards for years said they were unable to transfer the remaining balance to an NCMC card or obtain a refund while the existing smart card was still valid and usable.
Prakash H.S., a commuter from Jayanagara who recently switched to the NCMC card for greater convenience across public transport systems, said that he attempted to recover the balance in his old metro smart card but were informed by the Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) staff that a refund or transfer was not possible as long as the card remained usable.
“This creates a practical problem for passengers who want completely transition to the NCMC cards. In their case, the remaining balance could not be fully utilised because the fare for a regular journey was around ₹67, while the card required a minimum balance of ₹90,” he said.
Another commuter, Swathi Nayak from Dasarahalli, said, “The minimum recharge amount is ₹50, making it difficult to use the remaining balance precisely without either making an additional recharge or leaving an unused amount on the card.”
As a result, Ms. Nayak estimated that around ₹30 could remain unused, in addition to the ₹50 paid initially for the smart card, which is understood to be non-refundable.
While the amount involved may be relatively small, commuters argued that the issue was about the principle of retaining passengers’ unused money when they had moved to a newer and more widely usable payment system.
Meanwhile, the BMRCL officials said they would look into the issue and rectify it. However, they did not respond to queries about the corrective measures taken on this issue.

stories.headline: In-kind welfare: 22 crore move up consumption ladder
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: In-kind social transfers ranging from free foodgrains under the public distribution system (PDS) to laptops, bicycles and school uniforms have pushed nearly 22 crore people -- comprising around 19% of rural population and 8.4% of those in urban areas -- into higher consumption brackets, a new study in an NSO journal showed.
Using the household consumption expenditure survey (HCES) 2022–23 unit-level data, the NSO study concluded that 15.8% of the population at the national level saw improvement in their level of living as they moved into higher monthly per capita consumption expenditure (MPCE) category once the monetary value of free goods was imputed.
Which state saw most gains
Incorporating these welfare measures also reduced consumption inequality, measured by Gini coefficient, pointing to a boost in effective purchasing power as it freed up some cash that would have been allocated for buying some of these goods.
The findings also highlighted a distinct regional divergence in welfare impact. West Bengal led with over 40% of its total population (46.5% rural and 24.9% urban) transitioning to higher consumption brackets due to in-kind transfers. This was followed by Chhattisgarh (29.2%), Assam (29%), Karnataka (28.4%), and Uttar Pradesh (22.7%). In contrast, industrialised and higher-baseline states reported significantly lower transition rates, with Gujarat seeing only 3.7% population transitioning to a higher consumption bracket, followed by Kerala (4.6%) and Haryana (7.1%).
Despite concerns over several of such transfers being populist in nature, often announced ahead of elections, the study concluded that in-kind social welfare acted as a progressive measure as maximum upward mobility was concentrated at the bottom of the pyramid, indicating that welfare benefits effectively reach the targeted, lower-income households.
Researchers, however, noted that the 22-crore figure was a conservative estimate as major public services, specifically free healthcare benefits under schemes such as Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) and free school education were excluded from the calculations due to survey design limitations. Factoring in the out-of-pocket savings from health and education would indicate an even broader elevation of living standards across Indian households, it said.

stories.headline: ‘SC order won’t impact growth’: Yes Bank
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Yes Bank has told investors that Supreme Court’s order to restore Rs 8,415 crore of additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds written off during its March 2020 restructuring would not constrain growth, citing deferred tax assets (DTAs) and other capital buffers to absorb the impact. Rating agencies said the ruling would not materially affect the bank’s credit profile, although it has implications for its capital structure.
Crisil Ratings said Yes Bank could absorb the AT1 bond ruling’s impact through internal accruals and fresh capital, with support expected from its largest shareholder, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation. While the ruling is not expected to materially affect its credit profile, coupon payments for the intervening 5.5 years remain uncertain. In another case, Dhanlaxmi Bank was earlier allowed to defer coupons on Basel II-compliant tier-II bonds.
Analysts said reversing the AT1 write-down, originally credited to the profit and loss account, could leave the bank without the profits needed to pay coupons under the conditions of the AT1 bonds. As a result, the bank’s maximum liability was likely to be Rs 8,415 crore.
In an earnings call, managing director and CEO Vinay Tonse said the bank was examining the judgment and its options. 
“We respect the judgment and are examining it carefully, including the options available to the bank,” he said.
CFO Niranjan Banodkar said reinstating the AT1 principal would reduce the common equity tier-I (CET-1) ratio by around 240 basis points on a pro forma basis, based on an indicative assessment as of Sept 30, 2026, including profits. The overall tier-I capital ratio would remain around 13.7%, while the pro forma CET-1 ratio would be 11.4%. Banodkar said the bank was reviewing the judgment, legal options and capital plans.

stories.headline: Jio Platforms' anchor book draws record ₹2.5 lakh crore in bids ahead of IPO
stories.deck: The allotment of 7.24 crore shares at ₹1,119 apiece comes two days before the initial public offering opens for public subscription on October 21
stories.bodyText:
Platforms allotted shares worth ₹8,109.85 crore to 212 anchor investors at the top end of its price band, after institutional demand for the offering exceeded ₹2.5 lakh crore, more than 30 times the amount available in the anchor book, according to a stock exchange filing and people familiar with the matter.
The allotment of 7.24 crore shares at ₹1,119 apiece comes two days before the initial public offering opens for public subscription on Wednesday (October 21, 2026).
The strong demand underscores institutional investor interest in what is expected to be India's largest IPO, although the extent to which it translates into broader public demand will become clearer once the offer opens.
Life Insurance Corporation of India received the largest allocation, worth ₹499.98 crore, accounting for 6.17% of the anchor portion. New World Fund Inc was allotted shares worth ₹486.27 crore, followed by the Government of Singapore at ₹340.93 crore, SBI Focused Fund at ₹315 crore and BNP Paribas Financial Markets — ODI at ₹303.25 crore.
Domestic mutual funds received 2.489 crore shares worth ₹2,784.96 crore, representing 34.34% of the anchor book, through 95 schemes across 25 fund houses. Life insurers and pension funds received 97.4 lakh shares worth ₹1,089.95 crore, or 13.44% of the total.
Both categories exceeded the allocations reserved for them under the red herring prospectus dated October 14, which earmarked 33.33% of the anchor portion for mutual funds and 6.67% cent for insurers and pension funds.
Global investment firms participating in the anchor book include BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, Schroders, JPMorgan Asset Management, Franklin Templeton and Janus Henderson. Sovereign and public investment institutions include the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and the Monetary Authority of Singapore, alongside other long-term institutional investors.
Some large overseas and domestic institutions bid for allocations worth $750 million to more than $1 billion each, people familiar with the matter said.
Jio Platforms is seeking to raise about ₹30,213 crore through a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, at a price band of ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 apiece. The offering values the company at around $108 billion, according to the offer documents.
The IPO will open on October 21 and close on October 23.
Proceeds will partly be used to repay debt at its telecom subsidiary, with the remainder earmarked for general corporate purposes. Reliance Industries Ltd, controlled by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, will retain a majority stake in Jio Platforms after the listing.
Jio Platforms has grown into one of the world's largest mobile operators by subscriber numbers since Reliance entered the telecom market a decade ago.
The business has expanded beyond mobile connectivity into broadband, digital entertainment, cloud and enterprise services, making it the central part of Reliance's push into India's digital economy.
The company had 533.3 million subscribers as of June 2026 and carried nearly 60% of India's data traffic, according to reported company figures.
The listing will give public-market investors direct exposure to a business that has so far operated as a subsidiary of Reliance Industries. Its scale and the breadth of institutional participation make the offering a closely watched test of investor appetite for large Indian equity issuances.
The anchor book, which allows institutional investors to receive shares before the public subscription period, represents about 27% of the total IPO. Demand exceeding 30 times the anchor allocation, alongside subscriptions at the top of the price band, provides an early indication of institutional appetite for the offering.
However, strong anchor demand does not guarantee similar enthusiasm from retail investors or ensure gains after listing. Investors will weigh Jio's subscriber base and opportunities in digital services against competitive pressures, regulatory risks, capital requirements and its ability to translate scale into sustained revenue and profit growth, analysts said.
The offering also provides a measure of the Indian market's capacity to absorb a transaction of this size, with domestic mutual funds, insurers and pension funds accounting for nearly half of the anchor allocation. The public subscription will offer a clearer indication of whether that institutional confidence extends across the wider investor base.

stories.headline: India’s agrivoltaic capacity is expected to be more than 5-gigawatts in next 3-4 years: MNRE Secretary
stories.deck: “It is difficult to estimate but it should be upwards of 5-gigawatts in the next 3-4 years. It depends on state’s enthusiasm, ability to quickly notify a feed-in tariff,” said Union Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Secretary Santosh Sarangi
stories.bodyText:
India’s agrivoltaic capacity could scale to more than 5-gigawatts in the next three to four years subject to enthusiasm from states and their ability to notify feed-in tariffs, Santosh Kumar Sarangi, Secretary at the Union Ministry for New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) told reporters at a briefing ahead of the seventh Agrivoltaics World Conference to be held in New Delhi October 21-23.
“It is difficult to estimate but it should be upwards of 5-gigawatts in the next 3-4 years. It depends on state’s enthusiasm, ability to quickly notify a feed-in tariff,” said Mr. Sarangi.
Agrivoltaics entails the use of agricultural land for its primary purpose and solar photovoltaic energy generation.
“Once they (the states) are ready with feed-in tariffs. It would provide certainty to the farmer-producers organisations and cooperatives to make the investment decision. If states act quickly then 5-gigawatts plus should not be an issue,” he explained.
Mr. Sarangi added that the ministry had observed enthusiasm from state governments as well.
He also told reporters that several states, including Odisha, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh have conducted their own individual pilot projects for agrivoltaics.
Further, the Union New and Renewable Energy Ministry was also planning a scheme to support the states.
“We are planning for a central sector scheme which will support it (agrivoltaics). Probably we will make it a part of one of our existing schemes as and when those schemes are getting revised,” he said, “On that we are working with the Finance Ministry on how this could be done and how states could be incentivised to do different kinds of agrivoltaic models.”

briefs.headline: Harish Bhat resigns from Trent board after 12 years
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Harish Bhat, a long-serving Tata executive, has resigned from Trent, the retailer chaired by Noel Tata, citing growing personal and professional commitments.
Bhat, 63, served on Trent’s board for 12 years. An alumnus of BITS Pilani and IIM Ahmedabad, he continues to serve on the boards of Tata Starbucks and Infiniti Retail (Croma).
In his resignation letter to Noel, Bhat described his tenure on Trent’s board as a “pleasure and privilege”, crediting Tata’s leadership for the company’s rapid growth and transformation.
Bhat is the only member of former Tata Sons chairman 
Cyrus Mistry
’s inner circle to remain within the 
Tata group
 after Mistry’s acrimonious split with the conglomerate in 2016.
His resignation has revived debate about shifting loyalties within India’s largest conglomerate. Nirmalya Kumar, who also served on Mistry’s core team, wrote in a LinkedIn post that Bhat was “the first, and only member” of the group executive council “to switch sides to the new regime when Mistry was fired and go to the press with it”. Kumar argued that the move helped secure Bhat’s position during current chairman N Chandrasekaran’s era, albeit at a cost. “The reward was continued employment during N Chandrasekaran era with a honorific title but no power”.
As the balance of power gradually shifts towards Noel, some Tata group observers see Bhat’s departure as another sign of changing dynamics within the conglomerate. Kumar, who returned to academia after his stint with the Tata group, said the transition was prompting a fresh realignment of loyalties. “Now tables are turning from Chandra to Noel Tata and it’s time to sing praises to Noel Tata! Just like the Tata board, many of these political professionals are looking to unemployment!” he said.
During Bhat’s career with the Tata group, he held several senior leadership roles, including brand custodian at Tata Sons, managing director of Tata Global Beverages, and chief operating officer of Titan’s watches and accessories business.

briefs.headline: Tata Trusts row: SDTT files response to commissioner
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) on Monday filed its response with Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC) to complaints lodged by trustees Venu Srinivasan and 
Vijay Singh
, meeting the extended Oct 19 deadline for its submission.
The complaints sought an inquiry into SDTT’s administration and governance, including the appointments of Noel Tata as a perpetual trustee and his son, Neville Tata, as a trustee. They further alleged that Srinivasan was excluded from the decision-making process surrounding Neville’s appointment and questioned the involvement of SDTT and Noel in the commercial and strategic affairs of Tata Sons.
A Tata Trusts spokesperson confirmed the response had been filed but declined to share the contents of the submission, which runs into dozens of pages.
MCC had initially directed SDTT to file its response by Oct 12, but granted the trust additional time, extending the deadline to Oct 19.
The complainants had also sought interim directions, including the suspension or removal of trustees from SDTT, restrictions on Noel’s participation in matters concerning Tata Sons, and a bar on his exercising voting rights on behalf of SDTT at Tata Sons shareholder meetings. SDTT is the largest shareholder in Tata Sons, with a 28% stake, followed by Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) with 24%. 
MCC had barred SRTT from holding trustee meetings until an investigation into separate complaints filed by Srinivasan is completed. The latest complaints, filed on Sept 25 by Srinivasan and Singh, followed disagreements over the future of Tata Sons, including whether the company should remain unlisted and how liquidity should be provided to minority shareholder Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group.
Srinivasan had alleged that Noel had taken a direct role in identifying, negotiating and facilitating liquidity for the SP Group through the monetisation of Tata Sons shareholding.

briefs.headline: Crude holds near $110 per barrel as Middle East tensions keep supply concerns alive
briefs.deck: Currently hovering around $110 a barrel, oil prices are influenced by escalating geopolitical tensions involving Russia and Saudi Arabia. Washington's recent move to relax restrictions on Russian energy exports has shifted market impressions. Attacks claimed by Yemen's Houthis on Saudi facilities have further heightened stability concerns. As a result, prices remain resilient above $100…
briefs.bodyText:
Oil prices hovered near $110 a barrel on Tuesday as traders assessed the impact of Washington’s decision to ease some restrictions on Russian energy exports, while fresh attacks claimed by Yemen’s Houthis against Saudi targets added to concerns over potential supply disruptions in the Middle East.
WTI crude was trading at $98.72, up 18 cents, or 0.18%, while Brent crude stood at $109.70, gaining 16 cents, or 0.15%. Brent had climbed to $110.70 a barrel in the previous session, its highest level since May 20.
The market was weighing the possibility of additional Russian oil and fuel supplies following an executive order issued by US President Donald Trump on Friday night. The order waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs, including duties on Russian goods and penalties for purchasing the country’s oil and gas. However, Trump said on Saturday that he had yet to announce a final decision, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials needed more time to assess the situation.
Russia’s crude oil production rose by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million barrels per day, according to the International Energy Agency last week. Despite the increase, output remained around 870,000 barrels per day below the level recorded a year earlier.
The prospect of more Russian supplies has offered a possible counterweight to concerns about disruptions elsewhere, but risks to energy infrastructure in the Gulf region remain a key concern for traders.
Houthi attacks add to supply concerns
Fresh security concerns emerged after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they had carried out several attacks targeting Saudi energy, airport and military facilities. The sites named included an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha airport.
Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the claims, and Reuters could not independently verify them.
Separately, an attack by the Houthis on a government security forces training camp in Yemen’s Shabwa province on Monday killed 58 people and injured more than 200.
The latest attacks have added to concerns about regional stability and the safety of energy supplies, helping keep oil prices above the $100-a-barrel mark despite the prospect of increased Russian supply.

briefs.headline: Rising crude, lender-margin squeeze take toll on Dalal-Street
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Benchmark indices snapped a two-day winning streak on Monday, with 
sensex
 falling 876 points, or 1.2%, to 73,853 and 
Nifty
 declining 257 points, or 1.1%, to 22,889 as selling in private sector banks and IT stocks weighed on sentiment. Sensex opened 211 points lower at 74,518, while Nifty started 63 points down at 23,083. Selling intensified through the session.
Axis Bank
 was the biggest laggard among Nifty constituents, falling 4.2%. HDFC Bank declined 2.3% and Tata Motors lost more than 3%. On the other hand, JSW Steel gained 2%, ONGC rose 1.4% and State Bank of India advanced 1.2%.
According to Vinay Rajani, senior technical research analyst at HDFC Securities, Nifty is approaching support at 22,800, where it could resume its uptrend. “However, a decisive break below the positional support at 22,500 would weaken the bullish outlook and warrant caution,” he said. Most sectoral indices ended lower, with private banks, IT and FMCG among the worst hit. The Nifty PSU Bank index was the only sectoral index to finish in positive territory, gaining 2.5%, while the Nifty Private Bank index fell 1.9%. Union Bank gained 5.3%, highlighting the divergence between public and private sector lenders.

briefs.headline: Trade margins on 137 cancer drugs capped, but will bills get lower?
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Govt’s move to cap trade margins at 30% of MRP on 137 cancer drugs, covering over 1,000 medicine brands, puts the focus on actual patient savings, with effective implementation and monitoring needed to ensure it translates into lower medical bills.
The cap could narrow the gap between prices at which medicines are supplied to hospitals and their MRPs, but it may have a limited impact on overall cost of healthcare as hospitals may seek to offset lower margins by raising charges on consumables, diagnostics or procedures, public health and industry experts told TOI. A similar trend was seen after cardiac stent prices were capped in 2017, when several private hospital chains raised angioplasty package rates, they said.
What are the other charges 
Experts said wider rationalisation of margins across medical products, alongside closer scrutiny of hospital charges, may be needed to substantially reduce medical bills. Hospital stocks were down on BSE on Monday, following the govt notification on Oct 17.
The MRP of certain cancer drugs are up to Rs 5 lakh per vial or pack, including a combination of pertuzumab and trastuzumab, atezolizumab, teclistamab, inotuzumab ozogamicin and daratumumab.
“The success of this measure will, however, depend equally on timely implementation across manufacturers, distributors and hospitals. A trade margin of 30% should not be misconstrued as a 30% profit margin for hospitals. The defined trade margin applies across the distribution chain, and the basis of calculation and applicability of the prescribed margin at different stages of the supply chain, should be clearly communicated to avoid any misunderstanding,” Girdhar Gyani, director general at the Association of Healthcare Providers, which represents over 20,000 hospitals and healthcare providers, told TOI.
Oncology is a significant revenue stream for hospitals, with expensive cancer drugs and cost of care contributing to high treatment costs. The margin cap could put pressure on hospital earnings, raising concerns over whether lower margins could affect the viability of such services. “Affordability must be viewed across the entire cancer-care pathway, from screening and diagnosis to treatment,” said Mayur Sirdesai, co-founding partner at Somerset Indus Capital.
“The impact of TMR on affordability and patient access will need to be evaluated, said Sudarshan Jain, secretary-general of Indian Pharmaceutical Alliance.
Public health experts said the margin rationalisation may not be enough to reduce costs for patients. “Prices of these medicines will still remain out of the reach for many patients. Also, hospitals may find ways to hike charges of other items and packages,” said KM Gopakumar of Third World Network, a civil society group.

briefs.headline: India shelves coal import plan as high global prices, weak rupee raise costs
briefs.deck: India has decided not to mandate coal imports for power plants due to high international prices and a weaker rupee. Coal stockpiles have reached critically low levels at many power stations, prompting concerns about electricity shortages in the country. Policymakers are focusing on boosting domestic coal production and improving transportation to mitigate the situation.
briefs.bodyText:
India has shelved a proposal to make power plants import coal to replenish dwindling stockpiles, as elevated international prices and a weaker rupee have increased the cost of overseas shipments, Bloomberg reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the discussions.
The government had recently considered asking power plants to blend imported coal with domestic supplies to ease the fuel shortage. However, the proposal was put on hold because of the high cost of imports, the report said.
Policymakers have instead asked state-owned Coal India Ltd to increase production and the railways to ensure timely transportation of coal to power stations, according to Bloomberg.
The decision comes as coal inventories at Indian power plants have fallen to their lowest level in nearly five years, with higher electricity demand and reduced hydropower generation putting pressure on domestic supplies.
Coal stocks remain under pressure
Nearly half of India's power plants had critically low coal inventories as of October 17, with stocks below a quarter of their required levels, according to data from the power ministry.
A poor monsoon has kept temperatures elevated beyond the summer months, increasing electricity consumption for cooling and irrigation. Below-normal rainfall has also reduced hydropower generation, increasing the burden on coal-fired power plants and depleting their reserves.
India's electricity deficit surged in September, marking the worst power shortages for the month in nearly a decade.
However, the pace of coal stock depletion has slowed in October. According to Bloomberg's calculations based on power ministry data, domestic coal-burning power plants recorded an average daily inventory decline of around 48,000 tonnes during the first 17 days of the month, about a fifth of the rate seen in September.
The government expects electricity consumption to ease as temperatures decline and coal inventories begin to recover.
Average temperatures are forecast to fall slightly over the next two weeks, although they are expected to remain above the 30-year normal, according to the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts.
High import costs discourage overseas purchases
India has previously required power plants to import coal to supplement domestic supplies during shortages. However, benchmark thermal coal prices are currently at their highest level in three years.
The weaker rupee has added to the cost of imports, while higher oil prices have increased India's energy import bill, making overseas coal purchases less attractive.
The government had opted to focus on increasing domestic production and improving transportation instead of mandating imports.
The development follows an order requiring more than 100 captive coal-fired power plants to operate at maximum capacity from October 1 until the end of the year to meet an expected rise in electricity demand.
Government says coal supplies have improved
The coal ministry had said earlier this month that daily coal supplies to the power sector had increased by around 36 per cent from September levels and that the pace of inventory depletion had moderated.
According to a ministry statement, the designation of a plant as having “critical stock” serves as an early warning and does not necessarily mean that it is running out of coal or faces an imminent shutdown.
The ministry said plants with low inventories were being monitored closely, with supplies redistributed to support uninterrupted electricity generation.
Data from the Central Electricity Authority showed that 87 of 190 coal-fired power plants had critical stocks as of October 8, compared with 50 in the first week of September.
These plants held 20.6 million tonnes of coal, equivalent to 33 per cent of the recommended stock of 61.2 million tonnes.
The ministry also said rail loading had strengthened, averaging more than 465 rakes a day in October, with the target of 470 rakes achieved on three consecutive days. Supplies through road and other modes had also improved.
It said sustained coal transportation of 465-475 rakes a day should help stabilise inventories and support stock rebuilding ahead of festive-season, winter and subsequent summer demand.

briefs.headline: India probes Pernod Ricard, Diageo over Scotch whisky imports under UK trade pact
briefs.deck: Indian tax authorities are examining whether Pernod Ricard and Diageo wrongly classified bulk Scotch whisky imports for lower tariffs. The investigation follows reduced import duties under the recent India-UK trade pact that came into effect on July 15. Tax inspectors visited Pernod Ricard’s headquarters and searched Diageo’s offices regarding these classifications. Both companies claim they are…
briefs.bodyText:
Indian tax authorities are investigating whether liquor makers Pernod Ricard and Diageo wrongly classified bulk Scotch whisky imports to claim lower tariffs under the India-UK trade agreement, Reuters reported, citing five industry sources familiar with the matter.
The investigation centres on whether the companies were eligible for the reduced import duty introduced under the pact, which came into effect on July 15.
India agreed to cut tariffs on certain Scotch imports to 75 per cent from 150 per cent.
However, tax inspectors have argued that the duty reduction does not apply to bulk Scotch concentrates, four people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
“The tax department is concerned that bulk imports are being wrongly classified,” one of the sources said.
Last week, tax inspectors visited Pernod Ricard's India headquarters near New Delhi and questioned company executives about its Scotch imports, three sources told Reuters.
During the visit on Thursday, officials reviewed documents related to bulk imports, although they have not contacted the company again since, one source said.
Diageo's Indian unit, United Spirits, disclosed in a stock exchange filing last week that its offices at multiple locations had been searched on Friday as part of an “industry-wide exercise” by authorities.
The company did not specify the subject of the searches.
Two sources told Reuters that Diageo was also under investigation over the classification of some Scotch imports.
Companies say they are cooperating with authorities
Pernod Ricard told Reuters that it was cooperating with the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and providing all the information requested by officials. The company said it was committed to addressing any questions raised by the authorities.
Diageo also said it was cooperating with Indian authorities and had always complied with local laws. In its stock exchange disclosure, United Spirits said it had provided all documents and clarifications sought.
The investigation comes amid longstanding disputes between foreign companies and Indian tax authorities over import classifications and tariff payments.
Such disputes have involved companies including Samsung, LG and Volkswagen, with officials often raising substantial back-tax demands years after goods were imported.
India-UK trade pact cuts Scotch import tariffs
Pernod Ricard, a French company, and Britain's Diageo dominate India's $65 billion alcohol market, according to Reuters. Both import bulk Scotch concentrates, which are mixed with other ingredients to produce brands such as Royal Stag, Blenders Pride and McDowell's.
The India-UK trade agreement reduced import tariffs on certain Scotch products by half, from 150 per cent to 75 per cent, from July 15. The tariff is scheduled to fall further to 40 per cent over the next 10 years.
The lower duties have already led to price cuts for some imported Scotch whiskies in several states. Diageo and Pernod Ricard reduced prices by around 10-15 per cent for selected products in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Goa and Uttar Pradesh.
Brands affected included Diageo's Johnnie Walker Black Label and J&B, while Pernod Ricard sought approval for lower prices for Chivas, Ballantine's and The Glenlivet.
The British government said in July that “iconic UK products”, including whisky and gin, would benefit from India's tariff reductions. UK whisky exports to India were worth more than £200 million in 2022, according to the British government.
Crisil Ratings said this year that the UK accounts for nearly 75 per cent of India's imported spirits market, primarily driven by Scotch whisky.
Pernod faces other regulatory challenges
Pernod Ricard is also facing antitrust cases in India, its largest market by volume, as well as a $314 million back-tax demand over allegations that it undervalued certain imports. The company denies wrongdoing.
Diageo, meanwhile, agreed in August to reformulate some of its popular drinks after India's food safety regulator banned them in some states over the addition of flavours that allegedly breached regulations.
The latest investigation focuses on whether the companies' declarations for bulk Scotch imports qualified for the lower duties under the India-UK trade agreement.
