stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Bhavina Patel added another medal to her impressive career by winning bronze in the women's singles Class 4-5 table tennis event at the Asian Para Games 2026.
The Tokyo Paralympics silver medallist lost 7-11, 5-11, 7-11 to China's Zhang Bian in the semi-finals. The defeat ended her singles campaign, but Bhavina secured a bronze medal for India.
Bhavina was earlier named India's flag bearer for the Asian Para Games.
Bhavina Patel's journey
Bhavina has been one of India's leading para table tennis players. She made history at the Tokyo Paralympics in 2020 by winning silver in the women's singles event. It was India's first-ever Paralympic medal in table tennis.
Diagnosed with polio at a young age, Bhavina did not allow the condition to stop her from pursuing her sporting dreams. She began training seriously and won her first gold medal at the Para Table Tennis Nationals in Bengaluru in 2009.
She went on to establish herself on the international stage, winning silver in doubles at the 2018 Asian Para Games and bronze in singles at the 2022 edition.
Bhavina continued her success at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, where she won gold in women's singles. She was selected for the 2016 Rio Paralympics but could not compete due to technical reasons. 
However, she remained focused on her goal and reached the biggest moment of her career at the Tokyo Paralympics.
Bhavina has won more than 70 medals in ITTF ranking tournaments during her career.
In the 2025-26 season, she won 25 medals across singles and doubles events. Her tally included 17 singles medals — 12 gold, two silver and three bronze — along with eight doubles medals, including three silver and five bronze.
Apart from table tennis, Bhavina also works with the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.

stories.headline: UEFA gives FIFA November 2 deadline to release Infantino World Cup plan documents
stories.deck: UEFA submitted 42 detailed questions to FIFA, demanding responses by November 2 — 16 days before the nomination deadline for the presidential election next March 18
stories.bodyText:
UEFA has given FIFA a November 2 deadline to release documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s aborted attempts at a secretive investment plan for the World Cup and other governance issues.
The latest move in a power struggle between the two governing bodies came in the week after UEFA’s European delegates were disappointed by what they perceived as a lack of clarity by FIFA president Infantino over the issues at a FIFA council meeting last week.
Infantino provided no documents about the $4.2 billion World Cup sell-off plan he launched and quickly dropped in July amid a fierce backlash led by Europe.
Among the 42 questions that UEFA is demanding an answer to are: Infantino’s personal remuneration package, financial payments made to singer Marc Anthony, the handling of U.S. striker Folarin Balogun’s disciplinary case, business and political relationships involving Donald Trump and his family and the operational independence of FIFA’s judicial, electoral, and ethics committees.
UEFA asked U.S. federal courts to authorise subpoenas compelling the production of documents and sworn testimony about the abandoned investment plan called FIFA Forward Enterprise.
FIFA lawyers have claimed UEFA is harassing Infantino.
The formal letter, signed by UEFA general secretary Theodore Theodoridis on behalf of European FIFA council members, stated Infantino’s apology for his actions and subsequent explanation failed to address their core concerns.
“These explanations have not begun satisfactorily to address a number of fundamental questions raised by Council members. Others remain unanswered, and the information and documentation requested have not been (provided),” the letter said.
“The withdrawal of FFE, the recognition of mistakes, and the announcement of ‘potential governance reforms’ do not answer how the relevant decisions were taken or why the FIFA Council was not involved at the appropriate stage.”
UEFA submitted 42 detailed questions to FIFA, demanding responses by November 2 — 16 days before the nomination deadline for the presidential election next March 18.
With the next FIFA council meeting scheduled for Dec. 16 in Doha — after nominations close — UEFA insisted that answers cannot wait.
“These questions require answers now. They cannot be deferred until the next meeting of the FIFA Council — nor can future governance reforms substitute for scrutiny of decisions already taken and accountability for them,” the letter emphasised.
The earlier deadline would give federations time to assess FIFA’s answers — or its failure to answer — while they can still nominate or endorse a challenger.

stories.headline: Man City star Guehi says taking the knee has lost impact after opting against anti-racism gesture
stories.deck: ‘I don’t think it’s necessarily a football issue; I think it’s a wider societal issue and football is that beacon of hope to try to get the message out,’ said Marc Guehi
stories.bodyText:
Manchester City defender Marc Guehi believes the gesture of footballers taking the knee before matches might have lost its impact and wants to see more done in the sport's fight against racism.
Also read: The big blot on the beautiful game | On racism in football
Guehi, who is Black, didn't take the knee prior to kickoff in City's home game against Ipswich in the Premier League on Saturday (October 17, 2026) in the first of two rounds of games dedicated to the competition's “No Room For Racism” campaign.
It isn't the first time Guehi refused to perform the gesture, which was introduced in June 2020 to show support for the Black Lives Matter campaign. Since the start of the 2022-23 season, the Premier League has decided against taking the knee ahead of every match, with players instead invited to do so on certain occasions each season.
Speaking Monday (October 19) at a news conference the day before City's Champions League match against AEK Athens, Guehi said it was “great” that the Premier League's anti-racism campaign was continuing.
“Whether more can be done — more can always be done,” he said. “We have to see how we can move the campaign along.
“I don't think it's necessarily a football issue. I think it's a wider societal issue and football is that beacon of hope to try to get the message out. But whether more can be done, we will try, hopefully with the PFA [English footballers union], with the league.”
Asked whether taking the knee had lost its meaning, Guehi said: “Maybe. I haven't been taking the knee for a while now, to be honest. I'd always clap, just because of what that actually signifies.”
Guehi didn't go into more detail about his reasons for not taking the knee.
Another player not performing the gesture at the weekend was Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who stood while his teammates and opposition players for Manchester United knelt.
“Dom is more or less like, No, I don't go down. I show my respect by standing up, more or less,'” Leeds manager Daniel Farke said after the match, in which Calvert-Lewin scored in a 1-1 draw.
“I think each individual is different and shows respect for this campaign in a different way.”
In 2021, Wilfried Zaha — a Black player who was at Crystal Palace at the time — said he would no longer be taking the knee, describing the gesture as “degrading.”
“I feel like taking a knee is degrading,” Zaha was quoted by The Guardian newspaper as telling the FT Business of Football conference. “Growing up, my parents just let me know that I should just be proud to be black, no matter what, and I just think we should stand tall.
“I think the meaning behind the whole thing is becoming something that we just do now. That's not enough."
Premier League CEO Richard Masters said the current "No Room For Racism" initiative, which comes during the U.K.'s Black History Month, intends to use “the reach of our players to send an important message: we are united in the fight against racism.”

briefs.headline: 'I wanted to win this gold for my mother': Rinku Hooda triumphs amid grief at Asian Para Games
briefs.deck: At the Asian Para Games, Rinku Hooda triumphed by winning the gold medal in the men's javelin throw F46 category. This significant victory was dedicated to his beloved mother, who passed away just a month earlier. Despite the emotional challenge and a shoulder injury during training, he persevered with a strong resolve.
briefs.bodyText:
The pain of losing his mother was still fresh, and a shoulder injury had disrupted his preparations. Yet, when Rinku Hooda stepped into the arena at the Asian Para Games, he had one goal in mind, to win gold for the person he had lost.
The 27-year-old Indian para-athlete fulfilled that promise on Monday, clinching the men's javelin throw F46 gold with an effort of 65.11m. He edged compatriot Ajeet Singh, who secured silver with a throw of 65.02m, while Indonesia's R Saktyono took bronze with 55.30m.
'I wanted to win gold for my mother'
For Rinku, however, the medal was about much more than a place on the podium. It was a tribute to his mother, who passed away on August 8, leaving him to navigate personal grief while preparing for one of the biggest competitions of his season.
"I was a little disturbed in the last two months. My mother passed away August 8. I am still disturbed. It's okay from outside but it's not the same inside," Rinku told PTI from Nagoya.
"I wanted to win this gold medal for my mother. So, I would like to dedicate this gold to my mother."
Rinku barely had time to come to terms with the loss before returning to training. After completing the 13-day mourning period, he resumed preparations on August 19, initially keeping the intensity low.
"It happened on August 8. And on August 19, as soon as the 13th day (mourning period) was over, I started training. But I started lightly," said Rinku, who trains at the Rajiv Gandhi Stadium in Rohtak.
His preparations suffered another setback when he sustained a Grade 1 shoulder tear, forcing him to rest for around 20 days. The injury has since healed, although he continues to use taping as a precaution.
"I had an injury on my shoulder, a Grade 1 tear. Then I rested for around 20 days. I have fully recovered from the injury. Earlier, I used to do taping and stuff. I still do taping, but I didn't feel any pain," he said.
From a farming accident to the Asian Para Games podium
Rinku's journey in sport began against difficult circumstances. At the age of three, he lost his left arm in a farming accident when it became trapped in a paddy-sowing machine, eventually requiring amputation.
The setback did not take away his passion for sport. While helping his father with farm work, Rinku continued participating in school-level state running competitions. His introduction to javelin came through Amit Kumar Saroha, an Indian para-athlete who has mentored and coached several young talents.
Rinku announced himself on the international stage with gold at the Youth Asian Games in 2015, followed by silver at the World U20 Para Athletics Championships in Switzerland in 2016. He also competed at the Rio Paralympics that year, finishing fifth at just 18.
His medal collection has since grown steadily. He won bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games and silver at the 2022 edition in China. At the World Para Athletics Championships, he claimed silver in 2023 before winning gold in 2025.
The F46 classification is for athletes with a single above- or below-elbow amputation, or an equivalent impairment.
Paralympic medal remains the ultimate target
Despite his success at continental and world level, one achievement continues to elude Rinku, a Paralympic medal. He finished fifth at the Paris Paralympics in 2024, and the experience has strengthened his resolve to return to the podium at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.
"I have not won a medal in the Paralympics. So, that is my target now. I will focus more on that. The qualification for the 2028 Paralympics will start five to six months before the Games," he said.

briefs.headline: FIBA Women’s Basketball League Asia: Railways to become first Indian team at the event
briefs.deck: Four club champions from China, South Korea (KB Stars), Chinese Taipei (Cathay Life Tigers) and Japan (Denso Iris), along with Indian National champion Indian Railways and wild-card entrant Akari Sports from the Philippines, make up the six-team competition
briefs.bodyText:
Women’s basketball in Asia has a long history, dating back to the inaugural Asian championship in 1965. Even the Asian u-18 championship is 57 years old, while the u-16 Asia Cup is 17 years old.
Against this backdrop, the six-day FIBA Women’s Basketball League Asia (WBLA), beginning at the Sree Kanteerava Indoor Stadium in Bengaluru on Tuesday (October 20, 2026), is only in its third year.
Inspired by the women’s league in the Americas, the WBLA, however, hopes to grow.
In the WBLA’s two previous editions—2024 and 2025—two different teams from China won the title. This time, too, the Asian superpower looks strong enough to complete a hat-trick of titles for the country.
Sichuan Yuanda Meile, which won the inaugural edition in 2024 before Dongguan New Century claimed the crown last year, is back.
With a strong foreign presence in Chennedy Carter (USA) and Sara Blicavs (Australia), Sichuan appears to be the team to beat. The absence of its star player Han Xu is unlikely to dent its bid for a second title.
Yang Yi, Sichuan’s head coach, was confident of his team’s chances.
“The atmosphere for basketball is good in China. Our owner is very supportive. We are provided with all the facilities we ask for,” Yi told The Hindu in Bengaluru on Monday (October 19)through a translator.
Four club champions from China, South Korea (KB Stars), Chinese Taipei (Cathay Life Tigers) and Japan (Denso Iris), along with Indian National champion Indian Railways and wild-card entrant Akari Sports from the Philippines, make up the six-team competition.
While five teams have home-grown coaches, Denso has a Serbian at the helm in Vladimir Vuksanovic. In his fifth year as the club’s head coach, Vuksanovic wants to make an impact but is keen to take it one match at a time.
“We know the competition. China plays basketball at a very high level. They have very good foreign players. I want to build a young team from Japan with assistance from foreigners,” said the 54-year-old, who was an assistant coach of the Serbian women’s national team from 2016 to 2021.
Vuksanovic hopes the WBLA will grow like the East Asia Super League, with more teams and a longer duration.
Hosted by India for the first time, after the first two editions were held in China, the WBLA will see Railways become the first Indian team to participate in the league. Its head coach, Anita Pauldurai, knows the competition is of the highest quality and that her team faces a formidable challenge.
“We had a weeklong camp, which was too short. But still, we have prepared quite well. The WBLA will be good exposure for us. It’s a huge challenge. We will implement our strategies,” said Anita, who highlighted the urgent need for a National League to identify fresh young talent.

briefs.headline: Badoni walks the talk with his second double ton for Delhi
briefs.deck: On day two of Delhi’s second Ranji game, against Gujarat, Badoni amassed a career-best 217 off just 246 deliveries
briefs.bodyText:
In the build-up to the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season, Delhi skipper Ayush Badoni had explicitly stated his desire to rack up big scores in the First Class competition. It hasn’t taken long for the 26-year-old to walk the talk.
On day two of Delhi’s second Ranji game, against Gujarat at the Palam ‘B’ ground in Group C, Badoni amassed a career-best 217 off just 246 deliveries. It was his second double century for Delhi and third in all. As he was prompt to point out later, he had scored an unbeaten 204 for North Zone in the Duleep Trophy last year.
Having resumed on a score of 115, the middle-order stroke-maker, in the company of fellow overnight batter Sumit Mathur, made further merry on Monday as the host went on to compile 648 for six declared. The mammoth total entailed a 167-run partnership between Badoni and Mathur, who fell eight runs shy of a century. It was once Mathur holed out at cow corner off part-timer Manan Hingrajia that Delhi decided to declare.
While Delhi’s bowlers also had to toil in the final session, off-spinner Hrithik Shokeen snared the scalps of openers Aarya Desai and Abhishek Desai as the visitors closed the day at 98 for two in 35 overs. The latter was particularly unlucky to be dismissed, his flick hitting Sanat Sangwan’s helmet at short-leg and the deflection lobbing to Ayush Doseja at slip.
When Gujarat’s Vedant Trivedi and Hingrajia take guard on Tuesday, they will hope to take a cue from the manner in which Badoni and Mathur scored runs all around the ground. The key for the Delhi duo was to negotiate the first hour of play when Gujarat was armed with the second new ball. Once that was out of the way, Badoni, in particular, batted with utmost ease. The celebration, or lack thereof, appeared to be an extension of his nonchalance, with the all-rounder not even bothering to unstrap his helmet or raise his bat on reaching the milestone of a double century.
“When I take wickets, I enjoy that a lot. I celebrate wholeheartedly. When I score hundreds, I am not expressive,” was Badoni’s reasoning at the end of the day’s play.

briefs.headline: PSG-Barcelona match in Champions League to go ahead amid shock over France’s violent unrest
briefs.deck: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the possibility of calling off planned events was discussed, including football matches, ‘but this does not apply to tomorrow’s match between PSG and FC Barcelona’
briefs.bodyText:
The showpiece Champions League match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona will go ahead as planned on Tuesday in the French capital city, the French Interior minister confirmed, despite a weekend of protests marred by violence and looting across the country.
Also read | France protest: Prime Minister calls for localised curfews in cities to curb rioting, looting
Many French citizens have been left shocked by the images of violence that have drawn worldwide attention and highlighted the country's tense social climate. On Monday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he has instructed prefects to impose “very limited” and “localized” curfews in cities to prevent more rioting and looting.
The violence targeted city halls, other public buildings and hundreds of businesses across the country, leading to more than 2,000 arrests.
Tuesday's (October 20, 2026) match between PSG and Barcelona at the Parc des Princes will require a robust security deployment, with police forces already strained following weeks of student protests. In May, Paris police detained dozens of people after violence disrupted celebrations of PSG's second Champions League title win and a group tried to storm a police station in the French capital.
Speaking after an emergency meeting with top government officials, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the possibility of calling off planned events was discussed, including football matches.
“But this does not apply to tomorrow's match between PSG and FC Barcelona,” he said, adding that other matches planned in European competitions this week would not be affected. Nuñez mentioned the match between Lille and Galatasaray scheduled Wednesday in the northern city, where looters also vandalized shops over the weekend.
Nuñez offered his resignation on Sunday (October 18), but French President Emmanuel Macron asked him to stay to respond to police needs in an emergency situation. Macron instructed Nuñez “to take all necessary steps to ensure full transparency about the failures in planning and intelligence-gathering that led to the violence.”
Lecornu said details of the areas to be placed under curfew will be provided later.
Nuñez acknowledged that authorities had “lost control” in some major cities on Saturday (October 17), with hundreds of businesses looted.
